blocks.text: Nathan the prophet confronts King David with a parable of injustice: a wealthy man with abundant flocks who takes the lone ewe lamb belonging to a poor neighbor to provide for a guest. When David hears this account, he responds with righteous anger, declaring the rich man worthy of death and demanding fourfold restitution. Nathan then directly identifies David as this man. The narrative indicates that David's action regarding Uriah the Hittite and Uriah's wife has displeased the LORD, prompting the prophet's rebuke and the divine condemnation that follows.
